To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we present the first framework for lifelong learning that is capable of solving a stream of tasks with compositional structures, 2) our framework is general-purpose and can be applied to different domains and learning paradigms, 3) our approach is effective in learning to solve a stream of tasks, 4) our approach can be applied in both supervised and unsupervised settings, and 5) our approach can handle both discrete and continuous data.
we have developed a general-purpose framework that enables lifelong learning of compositive structures and that we show that this framework is effective for solving a stream related tasks.

we present a general-purpose lifelong learning framework that separates learning how to best compose existing components to solve novel tasks from learning how to adapt existing components to accommodate new tasks, and show empirically that this separation allows our system to achieve a good balance between stability and flexibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing general-purpose methods for learning compositional structures in the face of continual exposure to new tasks.
